fields.meta_title: Procurement Automation Built Around Your Policy | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Describe how you buy, and Emergent builds procurement automation for purchase requests, vendor quotes, and spend checks. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build Procurement Automation Around How Your Team Buys
fields.hero_description: Build procurement automation that routes each purchase request by category and flags spend that skips your contracts.
fields.features_subheading: Procurement automation runs each purchase by your written policy, from the first request to the order a vendor fills.
fields.feature_1:
Requests written in plain words

Staff describe what they need in a sentence. The app reads it into a category, an amount, and a cost center, then starts the approval path your policy sets for that category.
fields.feature_2:
Approvers chosen by category and amount

Software goes past IT security and services past legal. Anything above the budget owner's limit adds finance, and a reminder reaches any approver who holds a request for two days.
fields.feature_3:
Supplier quotes collected for larger buys

Above your quote threshold, one scope goes to several suppliers with a deadline. Replies sit side by side on one screen, and the buyer awards the work with every price in view.
fields.feature_4:
A catalog of contracted prices

Items you buy under contract sit in a catalog with the agreed price and pack size. Small orders from that list can go out as a PO at once, while anything off it goes to a buyer.
fields.feature_5:
Card spend checked against contracts

Card and invoice spend is compared weekly with the contracts your team negotiated. A purchase that went elsewhere for an item under contract goes to the owner of that category.
fields.feature_6:
Buying rules you can export as code

Your thresholds and approval paths export as readable code to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Every request and every order is a row in a database your team owns.
fields.why_description: Emergent turns your buying policy into a working app, with code you can export and keep changing by prompting.

fields.tab_content_1:
Every software request gets an IT check first

Priya Nair in marketing writes that her team needs 12 more seats on its design tool, about $2,160 a year. The app tags the request as software, finds the supplier on the approved list, and sends it to Tom Becker in IT security before the budget owner sees it. Nothing sits in a shared procurement inbox.
fields.tab_content_2:
Three supplier quotes land in one table

Facilities requires three quotes on anything over $10,000. For a yearly HVAC service contract, one scope goes to Northwind Mechanical, Globex Climate, and Initech Air. The replies come back at $14,200, $12,850, and $13,400, and Marcus Lee awards the work to Globex Climate.
fields.tab_content_3:
Under $500 from the catalog, the PO goes straight out

Lab staff order from a catalog of contracted items at the prices Cedar Lab Supply agreed to. Jonah Reyes picks four boxes of pipette tips at $38.50 a box, $154 in all. Catalog orders under $500 need no approval, and PO-3107 goes to Cedar Lab Supply as soon as he submits.
fields.tab_content_4:
A card purchase off contract reaches the category owner

Each Monday the app checks last week's company card spend against the contracted vendor list. A $640 office chair from a retail site is flagged, since Brightwell Office holds the furniture contract at $455 for the same model. Rosa Mendez, who owns furniture, gets a direct message with the $185 gap.

fields.howto_description: Seven steps to set up procurement automation that follows your buying policy, tested on last quarter's requests first.
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Connect the ledger and card feed
fields.howto_step_1_des: List every route money takes out of the company today: purchase requests, card buys, invoices with no PO behind them, and renewals nobody tracks. Start with the route that carries the most spend and has the fewest checks on it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Give each rule a dollar figure and an owner. Three quotes above $10,000, finance above $25,000, and legal on any contract that renews itself. Plain sentences are enough for Emergent to build the routing from.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Export the items your contracts cover, each with its unit price and supplier, from the contracts themselves or last year's orders. That list becomes the catalog staff order from and the reference the weekly spend check reads.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Connect the accounting system your team closes in, such as QuickBooks or NetSuite, and the company card feed. Suppliers and cost centers sync in first, and approved orders sync back with their cost center attached.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Have each decision arrive where the approver already works, in team chat or email, with the request and the budget left on that cost center. Name a backup for every approver to cover leave and holidays.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Pull 50 requests from last quarter, including the vague ones written in a hurry. Check the category each one was given and the approvers it reached. Correct any miss by prompting, then run the whole set again.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Launch with one area of buying, such as software, where purchases are frequent and the owners are clear. After a month, read how long each request waited at every step, then bring the next area on.

plan.angle: The top 10 are explainers and procurement vendors (IBM, AvidXchange, Ivalua, Precoro, Procurify) listing benefits in general terms. This page shows the procurement steps an operations lead builds for their own policy: a plain-words request triaged to the right approvers, a three-quote rule for larger buys, a catalog of contracted prices that small orders go through without sign-off, and a weekly check that catches card spend outside contracts. The purchase order lifecycle and invoice matching stay with the PO and AP siblings and are linked; procure to pay is explained in the FAQ.

claims_to_source: Procure to pay covers requisition, approval, purchase order, goods receipt, invoice, and payment
Off-contract spend is buying from a supplier outside the negotiated agreements; maverick spend is the broader term for noncompliant purchasing
A request for quotation asks suppliers to price clearly defined goods or services so the buyer can compare replies
Catalog or guided buying lets employees order from preferred suppliers at negotiated catalog prices
Three-way matching checks the invoice against the purchase order and the receiving record
Digital procurement applies software, data, and workflow automation across sourcing, purchasing, contracting, and invoice handling; e-procurement is the narrower transactional part
A procurement management system holds requisitions, purchase orders, supplier records, and contract terms in one place
Direct procurement buys materials that become part of the product a company sells; indirect procurement buys goods and services that run the business
